title: I did my first game ever 100% with AI from the ground up! Meet Batcula: the Flappy Gothic Arcade Game
author: Independent-Beach106
selftext:
Hey redditors! I just wanted to post my very first video game ever created entirely with AI with ZERO coding/development experience (all 100% vibe coding). So I will share below my learnings, tips, ideas and workflows:

1. Batcula was done solely through ChatGPT and Claude Code ( with some minor image cropping using Figma) + Suno for Music!  
2. I asked ChatGPT to think of a "2d flappy bird pixel style video game about a bat flying through Transilvania and the Carpathians and collects blood droplets and feeds on villagers to survive through the game, but also thing of a minigame that you have to do when you feed on a villager like tap quick, or a circular motion, etc"  
3. ChatGPT generated some screenshots of the video game which looked absolutely stunning so then I asked Claude Code to build me a video game based on the screenshots provided by ChatGPT  
4. Maybe I got lucky but the first rendition through Claude Code already played very smoothly and I just found it really addictive to play.  
5. I spent several days iterating and slowly adding more levels, backgrounds, obstacles, villager logic, scoring system and even the music!  
6. The parallax background was HARD WORK as I had to keep asking ChatGPT to render a background then separate the foreground from the backdrop etc (What you see in most of the levels in Batcula)  
7. The villagers were done entirely through iterating several frames of animations (example "Render 6-7 frames of Batcula feeding on this villager and save them on transparent background)  
8. I had no knowledge of hosting, deploying, etc so everything was a step by step walkthrough with the use of Claude.

Hope you enjoy taking Batcula for a flight and spot some hidden mechanics that I've added 😎 

Feedback is welcome, by the way!

I do have some feedback.   
Some blood drops are stacked on top of obstacles. That leads player to believe they aren't obstacles and lose.  


You should have mechanism that prevents blood from spawning on or close to obstacles.

replies.author: Independent-Beach106
replies.body: Good catch, I'll work (ask Claude to do it lol) on those
